notes: I attacked all 27 for wrong keys, defensible distractors, provider-dependence and stale facts, and could not sustain a flag against any of them. The two failure modes I was told to hunt hardest are the ones this batch actually guards against: every question whose answer turns on provider behaviour pins the provider or topology in the stem (046 names AWS; 047 names Direct Connect/ExpressRoute; 048 explicitly says 'Multi-AZ instance deployment (one standby)', which is the distinction that makes key A right and D wrong, since a Multi-AZ DB *cluster* has readable standbys; 053 states the two-minute warning rather than assuming it), and the ones left generic (045, 049, 054, 056, 059) have keys that hold on AWS, Azure and GCP alike. I verified externally: GCS Nearline/Coldline/Archive do carry a 128 KB minimum billable object size and Azure is introducing one for Cool/Cold/Archive from July 2026, so 045's option C is not an AWS-only artefact as I first suspected; CERT-In's April 2022 six-hour window (with 180-day log retention and NIC/NPL clock sync) is unamended and in force in 2026, so 061 is current; terraform plan does refresh from provider APIs by default, so 040's key A is right; and AWS documents that the Multi-AZ DB instance standby serves no read traffic, so 048's explanation is accurate. Two sub-threshold observations I am recording rather than flagging: 038's explanation says restarting a container is 'strictly the liveness probe's job', which overlooks that a startup probe failure also kills the container — true but immaterial to the readiness-vs-liveness contrast being taught; and 049's 'leaves the peak unchanged' is precise about peak concurrency while glossing that per-invocation open/close does reduce the sustained count held by idle warm environments. Neither changes a key and neither meets the brief's bar. The 27 explanations are unusually disciplined — each names its own strongest distractor and says why it fails — and I found no fabricated service name, section or specific. The empty flag list is a finding, not an omission.
